content: 5 min read Just now -- Press enter or click to view image in full size A raw timestamp, a raw byte count, a raw decimal fraction. None of those belong on a real user’s screen, and pipes exist for exactly one reason, to stand between what your data actually looks like and what a person should actually see. Most developers know two or three pipes well, and reach for a hand-written helper function for everything else, without realizing Angular already solved most of that formatting problem years ago, or that writing a matching custom pipe takes fifteen honest minutes. Eleven pipes. Each one tied to a real screen I have actually built, not a toy example invented for a tutorial. 1. date, for Anything With a Timestamp Real-world example An order history screen, showing when each order was placed, in the customer’s own timezone. {{ order.placedAt | date:'MMM d, y, h:mm a' }}{{ order.placedAt | date:'short':'America/New_York' }}The format string alone covers most real needs, and the optional timezone argument quietly solves one of the more common support tickets, a timestamp that looks wrong purely because it was rendered in the wrong zone.
